collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IV: ROMANCE, COURTSHIP AND WEDDINGS (LCD-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Crushes and courting on Isola: wondering whether someone likes you back, flowers and love songs, first dates, serenades gone wrong, proposals, weddings big and small, how many children, breakups and starting over.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager has written a terrible love poem: recite it anyway, or ask a friend to help fix it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has spent three nights writing a love poem for (friend). (subject.He/she) has just read it back, and it is awful. There is a line where (subject.he/she) compares (friend)'s eyes to two shiny fish. (subject) is fairly sure that is not a compliment. What should (subject.he/she) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) recites the poem at sunset, fish and all. (friend) listens with a perfectly straight face until the shiny fish, then bursts out laughing. Then (friend.he/she) says it is the best poem (friend.he/she) has ever been given, and that (friend.he/she) likes fish very much.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks the village storyteller for help. The new poem is beautiful, polished, and nothing like (subject). (friend) listens politely and says it is lovely. Weeks later, (subject) admits (subject.he/she) did not write it alone, and shows (friend.him/her) the fish version. (friend) likes that one much better.
